results.title: When Populist Rhetoric is High, Entrepreneurs Are More Likely to ...
results.content: Their dataset included measures of populist rhetoric from the Global Populism Database, data on the business ventures from the World Bank Enterprise Survey, and measures of national-level cultural tightness established in previous research. “The findings highlighted a clear relationship between populist rhetoric and informal venture entry across all types of economies,” says Michaelis. “Ultimately, the takeaway from a business owner’s perspective is that entrepreneurs are more likely to make a strategic choice to launch their businesses informally when their political environment is characterized by left-wing populist rhetoric,” says Michaelis. The paper, “Populism, cultural tightness, and informal venture entry,” is published in the *Journal of Business Venturing*. **Abstract:** This article examines how populist rhetoric and cultural tightness shape informal venture entry. Our results show that populist rhetoric increases the odds of informal venture entry and that this effect is magnified in culturally tight societies.
